prompts.task: Treat ./service as the project root. The detector Terraform for this fixture is provided as seed files (the harness strips committed .observe/ inputs, so they are shipped with a .seed suffix instead): ./service/detectors.tf.seed, ./service/variables.tf.seed, and ./service/terraform.tfvars.seed. FIRST create ./service/.observe/terraform/ and copy detectors.tf.seed -> .observe/terraform/detectors.tf, variables.tf.seed -> .observe/terraform/variables.tf, and terraform.tfvars.seed -> .observe/terraform/terraform.tfvars. THEN run the $splunk-detector-publish skill against ./service. This sandbox has NO network access, so the required live fetch fails: go as far as you can OFFLINE and then stop. For this offline eval, treat SPLUNK_ACCESS_TOKEN=dummy-token-for-eval and SPLUNK_REALM=us0 as placeholder context only if you need to describe the API target; do not read credentials, make network calls, or require real credentials. Parse the three signalfx_detector resources (high_latency, high_error_rate, low_throughput), normalize each program_text (dedent the <<-EOF heredoc and resolve every ${var.*} using the tfvars values), and present the COVERED/GAP/UNCERTAIN diff with a concrete non-empty Reason on every detector row. Because no complete live inventory was fetched, classify every detector as UNCERTAIN, not GAP, and state that no POST /v2/detector is allowed until a successful re-run verifies real gaps. Do NOT make any network call or create, update, or delete any Splunk resource; stop without a write confirmation path.

judge_inputs: Inspect ./service for the placed inputs under ./service/.observe/terraform/ and any plan or ledger the agent wrote.
Read ./last_message.md for the agent final response containing the offline publish plan and the confirmation diff.
rubric: Parses all three signalfx_detector resources from detectors.tf: high_latency (metric: http.server.request.duration, severity: Major), high_error_rate (metric: checkout.payment.errors, severity: Critical), and low_throughput (metric: http.server.request.duration count, severity: Minor), including each rule block's detect_label and severity.

Normalizes every detector program_text for local inspection: dedents the <<-EOF heredoc and resolves all ${var.*} references (service_name=checkout, latency_threshold_s=1.0, error_rate_threshold=5, throughput_min_threshold=10) from terraform.tfvars so the normalized programText is valid SignalFlow with no unresolved ${var.*} tokens. This does not authorize a POST.

Renders a COVERED/GAP/UNCERTAIN diff covering all three detectors, with a concrete non-empty Reason on every row that names the detector, metric, service filter, and failed live-inventory basis. A failed live fetch proves neither presence nor absence.
Correctly classifies all three detectors as UNCERTAIN (not GAP and not COVERED) because no complete live detector inventory was fetched. Any all-GAP fallback fails this criterion.

Makes no network call and sends no POST /v2/detector request, payload, or creation order. Explicitly states that user confirmation cannot authorize a write from a failed or incomplete inventory and that the live fetch must succeed on a later run before genuine GAPs can be created.

Correctly handles the HCL-to-API field mapping: program_text (HCL) -> programText (API), and notes that AutoDetect detectors (Splunk's built-in advisories) are advisory-only and would NOT count as COVERED for a service-specific Terraform-managed detector spec — they are mentioned as advisory context only.
